html:
In 1784 France handed the small island of Saint Barthelemy to Sweden in return for trading rights in Gothenburg. It stayed Swedish for almost a century.

Sweden made the main harbour a free port and named it Gustavia after King Gustav III. During the wars of the American Revolution and the Napoleonic era neutral ships traded there, and the island briefly prospered.

The boom faded, and in 1878, after a vote of the islanders, Sweden sold the island back to France. Swedish street names, a Swedish coat of arms and some old stone buildings remain. Since 2007 it has been a French overseas collectivity.
